questions.prompt: Can someone wear only a G-string and pasties at a licensed liquor place in Ada?
choices: Only if they buy a drink
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Liquor act, M.S.A. § 340A.101 et seq.

The provisions of M.S.A. ch. 340A relating to the definitions of terms, licensing,
               consumption, sales, conditions of bonds or licenses, and all other matters pertaining
               to the retail sale, distribution and consumption of alcoholic beverages are adopted
               and made part of this chapter as if set out in full. (Ord. No. 281, § 1, 6-2-81)

(a) The city council finds that it is in the best interest of the public health, safety
               and general welfare of the people of this city, that certain types of activities are
               prohibited as provided in this section, on the premises of licensed liquor, wine and
               3.2 malt liquor establishments, so as to best protect and assist the owners and operators
               and employees of these premises, as well as patrons and the public, in general. The
               council also finds that the standard set forth in this section reflects the prevailing
               community standards of this city. The provisions of this section are intended to prevent
               harm stemming from the physical immediacy in combination with alcohol, nudity and
               sex. The council also intends to prevent any subliminal endorsement of sexual harassment
               or activities likely to lead to the possibility of various criminal conduct including
               prostitution, sexual assault and disorderly conduct. (b) It is unlawful for any licensee to permit or allow any person or persons on the licensed
               premises when the person does not have his or her buttocks, anus, breasts and genitals
               covered with a non-transparent material. G-strings and pasties will not be considered
               sufficient clothing or covering for purposes of this section. (c) Violation of this section shall be a misdemeanor and shall be grounds for revocation
    …

questions.prompt: What counts as an alcoholic beverage in Albert Lea?
choices: Any drink that contains even a trace of alcohol
A beverage containing more than one-half of one percent alcohol by volume
Only beer, wine, and liquor sold in stores
Drinks that are at least 5 percent alcohol
questions.answer: A beverage containing more than one-half of one percent alcohol by volume
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Alcoholic beverages, Minn. Stats. ch. 340A.

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: Alcoholic beverage is any beverage containing more than one-half (½) of one (1) percent alcohol by volume. Applicant means any person making an application for a license under this chapter. Application means a form with blanks or spaces thereon, to be filled in and completed by the
               applicant as his request for a license, furnished by the city and uniformly required
               as a prerequisite to the consideration of the issuance of a license for a business. Cannabis is a dried preparation of the flowering tops or other parts of the cannabis plant,
               or a resinous extract of it (cannabis resin), smoked or consumed. Also called hemp,
               marijuana. Beer means three and two tenths (3.2) percent malt liquor which contains not in excess
               of three and two tenths (3.2) percent alcohol by volume. Beer store means an establishment engaged in the following types of business: restaurants, hotels,
               motels or bona fide clubs (on-sale only). As an incident to the business, cigars,
               cigarettes, ice, all forms of tobacco, soft drinks at retail and beer on-sale or off-sale
               may also be sold at a beer store. Brew pub is a brewer who also holds one (1) or more retail on-sale licenses and who manufactures
               fewer than three thousand five hundred (3,500) barrels of malt liquor in a year, at
               any one (1) licensed premises, the entire production of which is solely for consumption
               on tap on any licensed premises owned by the brewer, or for off-sale from those licensed
               premises as permitted in section [Minn. Stats. §] 340A.24,…

questions.prompt: In Blue Earth County, does a host have to be at the gathering to be held responsible if someone under 21 drinks there?
choices: No, a host does not have to be present
Yes, the host must be there in person
Only if the host owns the property
Only if more than 20 people attend
questions.answer: No, a host does not have to be present
questions.excerpt:
The board of commissioners of Blue Earth County intends to discourage underage possession
               and consumption of alcohol, even if done within the confines of a private residence,
               and intends to hold persons criminally responsible who host events or gatherings where
               persons under 21 years of age possess or consume alcohol regardless of whether the
               person hosting the event or gathering supplied the alcohol. The board of commissioners
               of Blue Earth County finds that: (1) Events and gatherings held on private or public property where alcohol is possessed
                  or consumed by persons under the age of 21 are harmful to those persons and constitute
                  a potential threat to public health requiring prevention or abatement. (2) Prohibiting underage consumption acts to protect underage persons, as well as the
                  general public, from injuries related to alcohol consumption, such as alcohol overdose
                  or alcohol-related traffic collisions. (3) Alcohol is an addictive drug which if used irresponsibly could have drastic effects
                  on those who use it as well as those who are affected by the actions of an irresponsible
                  user. (4) Often events or gatherings involving underage possession and consumption occur outside
                  the presence of parents. However, there are times when the parent(s) is/are present
                  and condone the activity and in some circumstances provide the alcohol. (5) Even though giving or furnishing alcohol to an underage person is a crime, it is difficult
                  to prove; and an ordinance is necessary to help further combat underage consumption. (6) A deterrent effect will be created by holding a person criminally responsible for
                  hosting an event or gathering where underage possession or consumption occurs. (Ord. of 8-9-2011, § 1)

               the following objectives: (1) To assist in the implementation of the City Comprehensive Guide Plan as amended; (2) To foster a harmonious, convenient workable relationship among land uses; (3) To promote the stability of existing land uses that conform with the Guide Plan and
               to protect them from inharmonious influences and harmful intrusions; (4) To insure that public and private lands ultimately are used for the purposes which
               are most appropriate and most beneficial from the standpoint of the City as a whole; (5) To prevent excessive population densities and over-crowding of the land with structures; (6) To promote a safe, effective traffic circulation system; (7) To foster the provision of adequate off-street parking and off-street truck loading
               facilities; (8) To facilitate the appropriate location of community facilities and institutions; (9) To provide human and physical resources of sufficient quantity and quality to sustain
               needed public services and facilities; (10) To protect and enhance real property values; and (11) To safeguard and enhance the appearance of the City, including natural amenities of
               hills, woods, lakes, and ponds.

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: Apron means a driveway area providing access to the property of an owner or occupant extending
               from a public street to the boundary of the property of said owner or occupant. Driveway/driveway access means the area of the right-of-way between the traveled surface of the road and the
               adjacent property that is intended to provide access for vehicles or equipment from
               the road to the adjacent property. Headwall means rock, concrete, masonry, metal, timber or other similar materials placed on
               the sides of an approach as support, to prevent erosion, or for decorative purposes. Junk means old or scrap hazard signs, copper, brass, rope, rags, batteries, paper, synthetic
               or organic trash, garbage, waste materials, rubbish, rubber debris, appliances, waste,
               or junked, dismantled, or wrecked automobiles or farm or construction machinery or
               parts thereof, iron, steel, and other old or scrap ferrous or nonferrous material. Right-of-way means the entire width between boundary lines of any way or place under the jurisdiction
               of the town when any part thereof is open to the use of the public, as a matter of
               right, for the purposes of vehicular traffic and is maintained by the town. Roadway means that portion of a right-of-way improved, designed, or ordinarily used for vehicular

               a gravel road is integral with the driving surface of a gravel-surfaced road. Vehicle means any device…

questions.prompt: If the City decides a mailbox was hit by its vehicles or equipment, what does it try to do first?
choices: Repair the mailbox and post to the condition they were in before
Pay you the original purchase price in cash
Replace it with a decorative mailbox of your choice
Have you file a claim with your homeowner insurance
questions.answer: Repair the mailbox and post to the condition they were in before
questions.excerpt:
The City has many operations that require various types of vehicles and equipment
               to work along the street gutter and curbline. During these operations mailboxes are
               occasionally damaged so this article provides a procedure regarding City repair and
               replacement. (Ord. No. 296, § 1(50.200), 4-23-2018)

For each reported incident, the City will conduct a review to determine whether the
               City will replace or provide reimbursement for the mailbox. Only mailboxes damaged
               due to the operation of City vehicles and equipment will be the responsibility of
               the City. (Ord. No. 296, § 1(50.201), 4-23-2018)

If the City determines that the mailbox was hit by City vehicles or equipment, the
               City will first attempt to repair the mailbox and/or post to the condition before
               the incident. If the mailbox and/or post is unable to be adequately repaired, the
               City will replace the mailbox as necessary with a standard size, non-decorative mailbox
               and replace the support post as necessary with a four-foot by four-foot decay resistance
               wood support post, both installed by the City. Alternatively, the mailbox owner can
               request reimbursement according to the fee schedule for the replacement of the mailbox
               and post by others, relieving the City of any further obligation. Mailboxes and posts
               shall be installed to meet U.S. Postal Service specifications for height and distance
               from the curb. In order to receive reimbursement, the mailbox must be inspected by
               the Public Works Department. (Ord. No. 296, § 1(50.202), 4-23-2018)

(a) In order to accommodate for conditions that may make mailbox installation for either
               the City or the mailbox owner difficult and/or not possible, the City has the discretion

               and consumption of intoxicating liquor, malt liquor, and 3.2 percent malt liquor are
               adopted and made a part of this Chapter as if set out in full.

For the purposes of this Chapter, and in addition to those definitions contained in
               Minnesota Statutes, Chapter 340A, as amended, the terms used in this Chapter are defined
               as follows: Brew Pub: The term "Brew Pub" means a restaurant that holds an on-sale intoxicating liquor
               license in which malt liquor is brewed or manufactured for sale and consumption on
               tap on the premises where the malt liquor is brewed or for sale and personal consumption
               off the brewer's premises. Brewer: The term "Brewer" means a person who manufactures malt liquor for sale. Display: The term "Display" means the keeping, storing, or permitting to be kept or stored
               of an alcoholic beverage which has been poured, dispensed or has had its package seal
               broken on, in, or at any table, booth, bar or other area of a licensed premises accessible
               to the general public, except when the alcoholic beverage is stored in a normal storage
               area during non-sale hours. Interest: The term "interest" as used in this Chapter includes any pecuniary interest in the
               ownership, operation, management or profits of a liquor establishment, but does not
               include bona fide loans; bona fide fixed sum rental agreements; bona fide open accounts
               or other obligations held with or without security arising out of the ordinary and
               regular course of business or…

               or unreasonable squealing or screeching sounds emitted by the tires of the vehicle.

               violation of this section shall include the unnecessary removal of the front tire

questions.prompt: In Waconia, what is it unlawful to do if fire hoses are laid in the street during a fire?
choices: Drive a car or other vehicle over the hoses
Park more than a block away
questions.answer: Drive a car or other vehicle over the hoses
questions.excerpt:
Subd. 1. Interference with city or fire department property. It shall be unlawful for any person or persons to interfere with or injure any property
               belonging to the City of Waconia or the fire department of the City of Waconia or
               to take or remove any of such property from buildings owned or occupied by the City
               of Waconia or the fire department thereof. However, the terms of this section shall
               not apply to firemen of the City of Waconia or other city employees while in the discharge
               of their duties. Subd. 2. Interference with fire hoses. It shall be unlawful for any person or persons to drive an automobile or other vehicle
               over any hose belonging to the fire department of the City of Waconia laid in the
               streets at the occurrence of any fire in said city or to in any other manner interfere
               with property owned by the City of Waconia or the operation thereof. Subd. 3. Interference with water lines, tools, and implements. It shall be unlawful for any person or persons to tap, cut into, or in any way interfere
               with any water pipe, water main, or sewer pipe of the City of Waconia or to take or
               carry away any tools or implements owned by the City of Waconia, without first obtaining
               permission from the persons having control over said property.

It shall be unlawful for any person, under any circumstances, to cause any false alarm
               fire to be circulated within the City of Waconia.

It shall be the duty of any person when so required by any persons having charge of
               fire apparatus during the occurrence of any fire within the City of Waconia or the
               surrounding area served by the City of Waconia Fire Department, to assist in operating
               any such apparatus or in extinguishing such fire.

The purpose of this chapter is to protect the public safety services…

questions.prompt: Can you drink intoxicating liquor in a Willmar park, sidewalk, or other unlicensed public building or outdoor space?
choices: Yes, if there is no admission fee
Yes, as long as you are 21
questions.excerpt:
The words, terms and phrases used in this chapter shall have the meanings ascribed
               to them in the state liquor act, M.S.A. § 340A.101 et seq., except where the context
               clearly indicates a different meaning, or except where a different meaning is specifically
               provided in this chapter, in which case the meaning shall be as provided in this chapter. (Code 1990, § 3-1)

No person shall give, sell, procure or purchase intoxicating liquor or 3.2 percent
               malt liquor to or for any person to whom the sale of intoxicating liquor is forbidden
               by law. (Code 1978, § 1209.15(1); Code 1990, § 3-2; Ord. No. 1305, § 1, 6-7-2010)

No person shall mix or prepare intoxicating liquor for consumption or consume intoxicating
               liquor in any public place not licensed in accordance with the ordinances of the city
               and the state law. For purposes of this section, the term "public place" means any
               building or outdoor space that is open to the public with or without an admission
               fee. (Code 1978, § 1209.15(2); Code 1990, § 3-3; Ord. No. 1256, § 1, 3-19-2007)

(a) No intoxicating liquor shall be consumed on a public highway or in any motor vehicle. (b) No malt liquor shall be consumed on any public highway or in any motor vehicle upon
               any public highway. (Code 1978, §§ 1209.15(3), 1210.07, subd. 2; Code 1990, § 3-4)

(a) License required. No intoxicating liquor shall be sold, distributed or consumed at the Willmar Civic
               Center Arena, referred to in this section as the arena, except at a function for which
               a license has been granted for the service or sale of alcohol pursuant to this section. (b) Application for license. The city clerk shall prepare forms to be used in the application for a license pursuant
               to this section. The city clerk shall also develop the rules and procedures for processing
          …
